mismatch.message: unsupported hero move: mon_arrive() with the hero's steed

summary: The v43 queue now stops at step 165 in dog.c:mon_arrive() after the accepted keepdogs() port. On descent, do.c:goto_level() calls losedogs(), which drains gm.mydogs through mon_arrive(With_you). C performs common arrival bookkeeping, then returns immediately when the arriving monster is u.usteed; it does not place the steed on the map. js/dog.js performs the same bookkeeping but throws at that branch. The next complete source stage is the contiguous dog.c family losedogs(), mon_arrive(), and mon_catchup_elapsed_time(); it must cover all three migration-arrival modes, failed-arrival cleanup, elapsed-time recovery, and the active restore/resurrection callers.

functions: dog.c:losedogs() (304-417), including shopkeeper scans, accessible-monster restoration, accompanying-monster arrival, migrating-monster arrival, and failed_arrivals requeue.
dog.c:mon_arrive() (420-624), including With_you, Before_you, After_you, Wiz_arrive, long-worm reconstruction, catch-up, destination decoding, placement, and failed placement.
dog.c:mon_catchup_elapsed_time() (627-723), including temporary-effect recovery, eating and special-use counters, tameness and starvation, leash cleanup, healing, and last-move update.
source.branch: The recorded case independently creates and tames a saddled pony, mounts it, descends, and reaches do.c:goto_level() -> losedogs() -> mon_arrive(With_you). At dog.c:466, C has already linked the steed into fmon, set arrival flags and hero coordinates, cleared mtrack, and restored its shape before testing mtmp == u.usteed and returning without map placement. The accepted v43 evaluation matched 165/166 screens and cursors and all 6320/6320 RNG calls; JavaScript stops at the matching step because js/dog.js throws instead of taking C's return.
callers: dog.c:losedogs() -> do.c:goto_level() (1816) and js/do.js:goto_level() (3068), which already awaits losedogs().
dog.c:losedogs() -> cmd.c:makemap_prepost() (1047) and js/cmd.js:makemap_prepost() (2634), which already awaits losedogs().
dog.c:losedogs() -> mon_arrive(Before_you) (371), mon_arrive(With_you) (383), and mon_arrive(After_you) (397); current JS js/dog.js:losedogs() wires only With_you and refuses migrating arrivals.

wizard.c:resurrect() (748) -> mon_arrive(Wiz_arrive); js/wizard.js:resurrect() (172) currently handles only the new-Wizard branch and is called by js/do.js:final_level() (3159). Wire the existing-Wizard arm through the do.js caller without claiming wizard.c:resurrect() as a whole-source port.
dog.c:mon_arrive() (495), restore.c:restmon() (1213), and wizard.c:resurrect() (738) call mon_catchup_elapsed_time(); js/restore.js:restmon() (583) currently calls a private, partial duplicate.
dog.c:mon_arrive() is private to js/dog.js today; make it the exported dog.c owner used by losedogs() and the wizard caller.
dependencies: Move the canonical mon_catchup_elapsed_time() implementation into js/dog.js, then import it in js/restore.js to replace the private partial copy. The current restore copy omits conditional RNG recovery for mtrapped/mconf/mstun, tameness and starvation updates, leash cleanup, healing, and mlstmv updates.

Wire wizard.c:resurrect() calls through the existing js/do.js injection boundary to avoid adding a dog.js <-> wizard.js import cycle; extend only the existing-migrating-Wizard caller branch needed to invoke mon_catchup_elapsed_time() and mon_arrive(Wiz_arrive).

The unported cross-file gaps are shk.c:make_happy_shoppers(TRUE) from losedogs() and dokick.c:deliver_obj_to_mon() from mon_arrive(); both C calls discard their void results. Keep mon_arrive() itself in this source port. Record note_unported() and skip only those two calls.

mon_arrive() uses return values from worm.c:get_wormno(), stairs.c:stairway_find_from()/stairway_find(), rooms.c:in_rooms(), mklev.c:somexy(), mon.c:mnearto(), and teleport.c:rloc(); existing JS owners are js/worm.js, js/stairs.js, js/rooms.js, js/mklev.js, js/mon.js, and js/teleport.js.

The existing js/dog.js relmon() is a migration adapter for mon.c:relmon()/mon_leaving_level(), not a completed mon.c port. Reuse it only for the list-transfer behavior it already represents; do not claim mon.c source completion.
The selected steed branch leaves MON_STILL_ARRIVING set when C returns early. Preserve this C state transition; do not clear it as a convenience.
tests: scripts/dog-migrate.test.mjs: pin full losedogs() list phases, arrival-mode dispatch, failed_arrivals handling, and mtrack restoration.
scripts/dodown.test.mjs: retain the do.c:goto_level() caller path for level changes.
scripts/restore-command.test.mjs: verify restore.c:restmon() calls the dog.c catch-up implementation rather than a private duplicate.
scripts/wizard-migration.test.mjs and scripts/leaving-level-helpers.test.mjs: cover the existing migrating-Wizard caller and Wiz_arrive path.
runtimeEvidencePlan: The admitted v43 case supplies the mounted With_you entry point through step 165, including the C early return for u.usteed. The accepted dog.c recording keepdogs-starting-pet-levelport is available as an ordinary follower transfer prefix; verify its arrival prefix against the new implementation.

Add an independent dog.c recording with a non-steed migrant whose stored destination selects Before_you, plus an After_you migrant, so losedogs() exercises both independent-arrival loops and mon_arrive() destination placement.

Add an independent elapsed-time recording in which a pet or migrating monster spends multiple moves off-level, then returns through mon_arrive() or restore.c:restmon(). Exercise an RNG-gated temporary condition and at least one tameness/healing update so mon_catchup_elapsed_time() is evidenced beyond its counter-only branch.

Add an independent wizard.c resurrection recording with an existing migrating Wizard, covering the direct mon_catchup_elapsed_time() and mon_arrive(Wiz_arrive) calls. Keep it separate from the new-Wizard constructor route.

evidence: Saved combined queue SHA-256 71e106e8eb6f63b838b78c59c3f25b455219162f1115104d7b8d23a1eca4cd36; its sole candidate is synthetic/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst, batch v43, case v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst, manifest challenges/manifests/v43.json (SHA-256 a4b2899d882bbae4e7283f771df1cab2f78dd6a32d7c0b19378a6d8cc5ab7400), recording challenges/cases/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst.session.json (SHA-256 bf2a99be1ce7847f948069f91419902d39e85ebb259933e2e8588791f1141472), and recipe challenges/cases/v43/v43-mounted-steed-stair-descent-pager-2-cfirst.recipe.session.json (SHA-256 4611748f3c7306188dcfdc6e07b89c010771192735e1b5fd4b320fea6c0c06ad). The current queue evaluates at 61ad0c2ff0d4cbd1e1d5ed0555e7550c6d34d983.
The saved evaluation reports 165/166 screens, 165/166 cursors, and 6320/6320 RNG calls. Its first mismatch is a stop at step 165: unsupported hero move: mon_arrive() with the hero's steed.

Upstream dog.c:304-723 was read as three complete contiguous functions. The step-165 call chain is do.c:goto_level() -> dog.c:losedogs() -> dog.c:mon_arrive(With_you). At dog.c:466, mon_arrive() returns for the hero’s steed after its common migration bookkeeping and before map placement; js/dog.js:1070 instead throws UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError.

Source call search found losedogs() callers in do.c:1816 and cmd.c:1047; mon_arrive() callers in dog.c:losedogs() at lines 371, 383, and 397 plus wizard.c:748; and mon_catchup_elapsed_time() callers in dog.c:495, restore.c:1213, and wizard.c:738.

The current JS arrival owner is js/dog.js:mon_arrive()/losedogs(). losedogs() refuses shopkeeper returns and migrating arrivals, and mon_arrive() refuses non-With_you arrivals, long worms, and the hero’s steed. The current catch-up owner is a private partial js/restore.js helper that has no tameness, starvation, leash, healing, last-move, or RNG-gated temporary-condition handling.

Source review found direct callers and required wiring: js/do.js and js/cmd.js already await losedogs(); js/restore.js contains the existing restore.c caller; js/wizard.js:resurrect() only implements the new-Wizard arm and js/do.js invokes it from final_level(). No whole wizard.c or restore.c port is claimed.

The dog.c source family calls make_happy_shoppers() and deliver_obj_to_mon() with void results discarded. The assigned port may record note_unported() and skip those unported callees; mon.c:relmon() remains represented by the existing migration adapter in js/dog.js and is not claimed complete.

Current recordings/dog.c includes keepdogs-starting-pet-levelport and keepdogs-escaped-pets-only, which cover pet departure routes. Neither establishes independent Before_you/After_you arrival, Wiz_arrive, or elapsed catch-up branches; the runtime evidence plan calls for separate recordings for those paths.
